title: The Case System — First Look (رَفْع / نَصْب / جَرّ)

steps.title: The name for what you've already been doing
body: Back in b1-u7 you named five roles — مُبْتَدَأ، خَبَر، فَاعِل، مَفْعُول بِهِ، مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ — on seven sentences. Every one of those words also had a specific ending, and you got it right every time without naming the system: that ending is its case (إِعْرَاب), and there are only three. رَفْع (nominative) is ḍamma ـُ or tanwīn ـٌ — مُبْتَدَأ، خَبَر، and فَاعِل are always رَفْع. نَصْب (accusative) is fatḥa ـَ or tanwīn ـً — مَفْعُول بِهِ is always نَصْب, and so is gr:kana's predicate and every sister of إنّ's subject. جَرّ (genitive) is kasra ـِ or tanwīn ـٍ — مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ is always جَرّ, and so is any noun after a preposition.
This lesson reuses the exact same seven sentences from role recognition. Nothing new to read — just naming, for the first time, the case ending that was already sitting on every word you tagged.

This first look covers only regular nouns — the ones that take a plain ḍamma/fatḥa/kasra. Two irregular layers (diptotes, and the five nouns / sound plurals, which use a long vowel instead) are still ahead.

steps.title: Two words, two roles, two cases
steps.prompt: الرَّجُلِ and كَبِيرٌ each have a role and a case here. Which pair is correct?
steps.explanation: الرَّجُلِ is the possessor here, so its role is مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ, which is always جَرّ regardless of context. The whole phrase بَيْتُ الرَّجُلِ together forms the sentence's topic, its مُبْتَدَأ; كَبِيرٌ, describing it, is the predicate — the خَبَر — which is رَفْع.

steps.title: Two words, two roles, two cases
steps.prompt: الطَّالِبِ and جَدِيدٌ each have a role and a case here. Which pair is correct?
steps.explanation: الطَّالِبِ is the possessor, so it is مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ, always جَرّ, no matter where the phrase sits in the sentence. جَدِيدٌ, the predicate describing قَلَمُ الطَّالِبِ, is the خَبَر, which is رَفْع.

steps.title: You've parsed your first sentences
steps.message: رَفْع، نَصْب، جَرّ — the three cases, on words whose roles you already knew. Diptotes, the five nouns, sound-plural markers, and verb mood are still ahead — this was the regular system, the foundation the rest builds on.
